# Claude.ai Documentation

- [Welcome](https://claude.com/docs/index.md): Connect Claude to your tools, teach it how your team works, and put it to work in Slack, on your desktop, in Microsoft 365, or through the Claude API.
- [Connectors, skills, and plugins](https://claude.com/docs/extend/overview.md): Choose how to customize Claude: MCP connectors give it access to your tools, skills teach it how you do a task, and plugins package both as one install.
- [Plugins](https://claude.com/docs/plugins/overview.md): Add plugins to Claude: what a plugin adds, where to find and install one, and where it's available across chat, Cowork, and Claude Code.
- [Create a plugin with Claude](https://claude.com/docs/plugins/create-with-claude.md): Make a plugin for your own workflow from claude.ai or the desktop app without writing files: choose Create with Claude and answer Claude's questions.
- [Share a plugin with teammates](https://claude.com/docs/plugins/share.md): Share a plugin you made with specific people in your Team or Enterprise organization, or publish it to your organization's library.
- [Get started with connectors](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/getting-started.md): Connect Claude to an app or service from the Connectors directory, turn the connector on in a conversation, and manage or disconnect it later.
- [Connectors directory](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/directory.md): Browse verified and community MCP connectors in the Connectors Directory, one catalog for claude.ai, Claude Desktop, mobile, Claude Code, and Cowork
- [Add a connector that isn't in the directory](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/custom/add-unlisted.md): Connect Claude to an MCP server that isn't in the Connectors Directory, by its URL or as a local desktop extension.
- [Connector verification](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/verification.md): How Anthropic reviews connectors in the directory, what the Verified, Community, and Custom labels mean, and how to stay safe with third-party connectors.
- [Google Drive](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/google/drive.md): Connect the Google Drive connector so Claude can search your Drive, read Docs, Sheets, Slides, and PDFs, and use Drive files in chats and projects.
- [Gmail](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/google/gmail.md): Connect the Gmail connector so Claude can search your email and answer questions from your messages, with citations back to each one.
- [Google Calendar](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/google/calendar.md): Connect the Google Calendar connector so Claude can answer questions about your meetings, attendees, and availability.
- [Microsoft 365 connector](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/microsoft/365.md): Connect SharePoint, OneDrive, Outlook, and Teams to Claude so it can search, analyze, and act on your Microsoft 365 information
- [GitHub integration](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/github/index.md): Add a GitHub repository to a conversation, or files and folders from a repository to a project, so Claude can read your code
- [Slack integration](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/slack/index.md): Use Claude directly in your Slack workspace with the Claude in Slack app, and let Claude search Slack with the Slack connector
- [Skills overview](https://claude.com/docs/skills/overview.md): Find, turn on, and use skills: directories of instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude loads to handle specific tasks
- [Create custom skills](https://claude.com/docs/skills/how-to.md): Create a custom skill for Claude: write the SKILL.md file, add resources and scripts, package the skill, and test it.
- [Manage plugins for your organization](https://claude.com/docs/plugins/admin.md): Control which plugins members of your Team or Enterprise organization can use in claude.ai and Cowork: see what you have, add your own, and set availability.
- [Sync your organization's plugins from a repository](https://claude.com/docs/plugins/org-sync.md): Distribute your organization's plugins from a GitHub or GitLab repository through organization settings, including repository requirements and GitLab setup.
- [Roll out a plugin to your whole organization](https://claude.com/docs/plugins/org-rollout.md): Get your organization's plugin to members in claude.ai and Cowork and to developers in Claude Code by using organization settings and managed settings together.
- [MCP tunnels](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/mcp-tunnels/overview.md): Connect Claude to MCP servers inside your private network without opening inbound firewall ports or exposing the servers to the internet.
- [Set up an MCP tunnel](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/mcp-tunnels/setup.md): Create a Tunnels API key, deploy the MCP tunnel stack with Helm or Docker Compose, verify the connection, and add tunneled MCP servers as custom connectors.
- [Authenticate to MCP servers behind a tunnel](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/mcp-tunnels/oauth.md): Make OAuth sign-in work for MCP servers reached through an MCP tunnel when the authorization server or identity provider is inside your network.
- [Troubleshoot MCP tunnels](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/mcp-tunnels/troubleshooting.md): Fix MCP tunnel problems: cloudflared won't connect, tools don't appear, routing and IP validation errors, TLS and certificate failures, and OAuth errors.
- [Build for Claude](https://claude.com/docs/build/overview.md): Build a plugin people use inside Claude: an MCP connector to your product, skills for your workflows, optional MCP Apps UI, and a listing in the directory.
- [Decide what to include in your plugin](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/what-to-build.md): Decide which pieces your Claude plugin needs: an MCP connector backed by a server you host, skills, commands, agents, or UI, and how they're listed together.
- [Build your first plugin](https://claude.com/docs/plugins/quickstart.md): Build a plugin with one skill and an optional MCP connector, test it in Claude Code, validate it, and push it to GitHub, ready to submit your own.
- [Plugin structure and testing](https://claude.com/docs/plugins/build.md): Reference for the plugin folder: what each file is, the manifest fields every app reads, bundling an MCP connector with its skill, and testing on each app.
- [Plugin feature support across platforms](https://claude.com/docs/plugins/platform-support.md): Look up which plugin components and install paths work in claude.ai chat, Cowork, and Claude Code, and why a plugin behaves differently on each.
- [Build an MCP server for Claude](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/index.md): Build a remote MCP server that people use as a connector in Claude: where it runs, authentication, what it exposes, size and timeout limits, and distribution.
- [Build your first MCP server for Claude](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/quickstart.md): Build a minimal MCP server with one tool in JavaScript, run it on your machine, and connect it to Claude Code so Claude calls your tool.
- [Authentication for connectors](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/authentication.md): Meet Claude's OAuth requirements for remote MCP servers: supported authentication types, client registration, discovery, callback URLs, and token refresh.
- [Lazy authentication for MCP servers](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/lazy-authentication.md): Let users call public tools immediately and defer OAuth until a protected tool is actually invoked.
- [Enterprise Managed Auth for connectors](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/enterprise-managed-auth.md): Support auto-connect in Claude by accepting identity assertions from a customer's identity provider or from Claude, so users skip the OAuth consent step.
- [Test your connector](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/testing.md): Test your MCP server against Claude as a custom connector before you submit it to the directory, including a local server exposed through a tunnel.
- [Troubleshoot your connector](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/troubleshooting.md): Diagnose and resolve common connection, authorization, and tool-call failures for custom and directory MCP connectors
- [Build a desktop extension with MCPB](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/mcpb.md): Package a local MCP server as a single-click .mcpb install for Claude Desktop: when to build one, the CLI quickstart, manifest.json, and how users install it.
- [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/mcp.md): Get oriented to the Model Context Protocol, the open standard behind Claude's connectors: local and remote servers, tools, resources, and prompts.
- [Get started with MCP Apps](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/mcp-apps/getting-started.md): See what an MCP App can do in Claude, such as the side panel, app tools, and embedded websites, then try an example and build your own with the SDK.
- [Add an interactive UI to your MCP server](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/mcp-apps/quickstart.md): Add an MCP App to the quickstart MCP server: register a ui:// resource with the MCP Apps SDK, link it to a tool, and check that the server advertises the UI.
- [Design guidelines](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/mcp-apps/design-guidelines.md): Design MCP Apps that feel native to Claude: display modes, mobile layout, visual style, interaction patterns, and the host's style variables.
- [Show your MCP App in the side panel or full screen](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/mcp-apps/display-modes.md): Move your MCP App from the conversation to the side panel or full screen. Declare display modes, request a mode, and lay out by the size Claude reports.
- [Let people open your MCP App without asking Claude](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/mcp-apps/entry-points.md): Mark a tool as a global entry point so people can open your MCP App from the Artifacts page in Claude, and check why it might not appear.
- [Let Claude call tools in your MCP App](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/mcp-apps/app-tools.md): Register tools in your MCP App so that Claude can change what's on screen. Test a tool and fix SDK errors.
- [Send messages to Claude from your MCP App](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/mcp-apps/send-messages.md): Send a message from your MCP App's view to Claude with app.sendMessage. Handle each result, and keep messages within what Claude accepts.
- [Embed a website in an MCP App](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/mcp-apps/embedded-sites.md): Embed your own website in an MCP App. Declare its origin in frameDomains, check whether it loads for your connector, and set your site's frame-ancestors header.
- [Download files from your MCP App](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/mcp-apps/download-files.md): Save a file from your MCP App to the user's device with app.downloadFile. Handle the result, fix rejected requests, and avoid refused file types.
- [Blend your MCP App with Claude's theme](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/mcp-apps/transparent-theming.md): Make your MCP App's background transparent and style it with Claude's host style variables so it blends into the conversation in light and dark mode.
- [Supersede older widget instances](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/mcp-apps/instance-supersession.md): Keep only the newest copy of an MCP App widget active when Claude calls its tool more than once in a conversation, using a server key and BroadcastChannel.
- [Open external links from MCP Apps](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/mcp-apps/external-links.md): Declare allowed link destinations so ui/open-link requests from your directory connector's MCP App open without Claude's confirmation modal.
- [Troubleshoot MCP Apps](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/mcp-apps/troubleshooting.md): Debug MCP Apps in Claude with developer tools on desktop and iOS, and fix invisible apps, large tool results, iOS-only request failures, and ui.domain errors.
- [Publish to the directory](https://claude.com/docs/directory/publish.md): Submit a plugin or MCP connector to Anthropic's directory: the two submission kinds, who can submit, what review involves, and where to start.
- [Directory connectors vs custom connectors](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/directory-vs-custom.md): Compare directory-listed and custom connectors: Anthropic review, in-product discovery, install links, Suggested Connectors, and per-tenant URL listings.
- [Plugin pre-submission checklist](https://claude.com/docs/plugins/pre-submission-checklist.md): Fix every finding before you submit a plugin to the Claude plugin directory: what the developer portal's validation and scan check, and what each result means.
- [Submit your plugin](https://claude.com/docs/plugins/submit.md): Submit a plugin from a GitHub repository to Anthropic's directory through the developer portal, follow its review, publish it, and release updates.
- [Connector pre-submission checklist](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/review-criteria.md): Check your MCP connector against what Anthropic reviewers test, including tool design, prompt-injection patterns, and functional quality, before you submit.
- [Submit a connector to the directory](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/submission.md): Submit a remote MCP server or MCP App to the Connectors Directory through the developer portal: requirements, screenshot specs, and what each step asks for.
- [Track your directory submission](https://claude.com/docs/directory/submission-status.md): Look up the status the developer portal shows for a plugin bundle or MCP connector submission: what it means, who acts next, and who to contact.
- [Manage your listing after publishing](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/after-publishing.md): Update your MCP server, plugin, and directory listing after publication, keep your listing URL stable, and delist when you need to.
- [Manage your directory listing](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/managing-your-listing.md): Track submissions, monitor server health and usage metrics, and edit your directory listing
- [Overview](https://claude.com/docs/cowork/overview.md): Learn about Cowork, Anthropic's agentic workspace
- [Changelog](https://claude.com/docs/cowork/changelog.md): Release notes for Claude Desktop
- [Run tasks in the background with Dispatch](https://claude.com/docs/cowork/guide/dispatch.md): Assign work to a Dispatch agent that plans, runs, and reports on tasks while you do something else, on this computer or from your phone.
- [Network access for shell commands](https://claude.com/docs/cowork/guide/network-access.md): Which hosts the shell commands in a Cowork task can reach, and what works on package registries and GitHub.
- [Install plugins](https://claude.com/docs/cowork/guide/plugins.md): Add packaged skills, connectors, and agents to Cowork from the plugin marketplace or a file.
- [Organize work with projects](https://claude.com/docs/cowork/guide/projects.md): Group folders, instructions, and context into a Cowork project so Claude starts each session with the right setup.
- [Monitoring](https://claude.com/docs/cowork/monitoring.md): Track Cowork usage and activity across your organization with OpenTelemetry
- [Set up Cowork (local mode) for a HIPAA-ready organization](https://claude.com/docs/cowork/hipaa-setup.md): Prepare members' computers to run Cowork (local mode) under the HIPAA configuration. Covers the Claude Desktop policy, network limits, and local data.
- [Work with Claude Tag](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/overview.md): Claude Tag puts Claude in your Slack channels with admin-governed access. See what to hand it, how setup works, and where to start as an admin or end user.
- [How Claude Tag works](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/concepts/how-it-works.md): Each Claude Tag thread in Slack runs a working session in a sandbox. See how progress shows in the thread, how to steer mid-task, what survives between turns, and how memory is scoped.
- [Glossary](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/concepts/glossary.md): Claude Tag terms defined in one place, including agent identity, bundle, connector, personal connector, scope, Agent Proxy, routine, and session.
- [How agent identity works](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/concepts/agent-identity.md): Claude Tag acts under its own service accounts in Slack channels, not as you. See how channel access is bounded, how credentials reach it, how Claude uses your personal connectors for your own tasks in a channel, and why DMs differ.
- [Personal connectors in channels](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/concepts/personal-connectors.md): Claude can use your own claude.ai connectors, called personal connectors, for your tasks in a Slack channel. See how you approve connector use, when Claude asks you to review a result before posting it, and what other people in the channel can reach.
- [Security and data handling](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/concepts/security-and-data.md): How Claude Tag keeps credentials out of the sandbox, limits where a channel session's requests can go, and controls who can see artifacts and invoke Claude.
- [Data lifecycle and deletion](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/concepts/data-lifecycle.md): What Claude Tag stores on Anthropic's side, how long session transcripts and memory are kept, and what disconnecting a workspace, uninstalling the app, deleting a Slack channel, removing a scope, or leaving the organization does to that data.
- [What the Claude Slack app can access](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/for-slack-admins.md): What the Claude app reads and posts in Slack, the OAuth scopes it requests, and what installing it does not grant. Written for the Slack admin approving the install.
- [Set up Claude Tag](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/setup-overview.md): Set up Claude Tag for your organization: pair your Slack workspace, add Claude to channels, launch, give Claude access to your tools, and check that it works.
- [Give Claude access to your tools](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/add-connections.md): Add connectors so Claude Tag acts in your tools with its own credentials. Covers service accounts, bundles, allowed websites, domain entries, and plugins.
- [Configure GitHub access](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/configure-github.md): Give Claude its own GitHub identity through the Claude GitHub App. Covers linking your GitHub organization, granting repositories, and GitHub Actions.
- [Configure GitLab access](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/configure-gitlab.md): Give Claude its own GitLab identity to read projects, manage issues, review merge requests, and check pipelines. Covers the account, token, and connector.
- [Set a spend limit](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/set-spend-limit.md): Claude Tag channel work bills to your organization's usage balance. Set the spend limit and see what happens when it's reached.
- [Set up Claude Tag for on-call](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/setup-oncall.md): Put Claude on call for incident response in Slack: run setup at claude.ai/oncall, pick or auto-join incident channels, cap spend, and deploy.
- [Per-service connection guides](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/overview.md): Step-by-step setup for each tool Claude Tag can connect to. Each guide covers the dedicated account to create, the credential to enter, and the URL to allow.
- [Connect a service that isn't in the list](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/custom.md): Connect a tool that isn't in Claude Tag's connector list. Covers credential types, what each form field means, and how to add a custom MCP server.
- [Connect Amplitude](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/amplitude.md): Connect Amplitude to Claude Tag with a project API key and secret key, or by signing in with Amplitude, so Claude can answer product-analytics questions.
- [Connect Asana](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/asana.md): Connect Asana to Claude Tag so it can file tasks and read project status. Covers the dedicated account to create, the token fields, and the URL to allow.
- [Connect Jira and Confluence](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/atlassian.md): Connect Atlassian Cloud to Claude Tag so it can read and update Jira issues and search Confluence pages.
- [Connect BigQuery](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/bigquery.md): Connect BigQuery to Claude Tag so it can run read-only queries on your datasets, using a GCP service-account key.
- [Connect Datadog](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/datadog.md): Connect Datadog to Claude Tag so it can query metrics, logs, and monitors. Covers the dedicated account to create, the API key fields, and the URL to allow.
- [Connect GitLab](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/gitlab.md): Connect GitLab to Claude Tag so it can read code, manage issues, comment on merge requests, and check pipelines through the GitLab API. Covers token permissions, self-managed hostnames, and how it differs from GitHub.
- [Connect Gong](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/gong.md): Connect Gong to Claude Tag so it can pull call summaries and deal context. Covers the dedicated account to create, the token fields, and the URL to allow.
- [Connect Google Drive, Calendar, and Gmail](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/google.md): Connect Google Drive, Calendar, and Gmail to Claude Tag so it can read docs, sheets, events, and email. Covers OAuth setup, the service-account option, and what each grants.
- [Connect HubSpot](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/hubspot.md): Connect HubSpot to Claude Tag so it can read pipeline, deal, and contact data. Covers the dedicated account to create, the token fields, and the URL to allow.
- [Connect Linear](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/linear.md): Connect Linear to Claude Tag so it can file tickets and post status updates. Covers the dedicated account to create, the token fields, and the URL to allow.
- [Connect Notion](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/notion.md): Connect Notion to Claude Tag so it can read and search your Notion workspace. Covers the dedicated account to create, the token fields, and the URL to allow.
- [Connect PagerDuty](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/pagerduty.md): Connect PagerDuty to Claude Tag so it can read incidents and on-call schedules. Covers the dedicated account to create, the token fields, and the URL to allow.
- [Connect Salesforce](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/salesforce.md): Connect Salesforce to Claude Tag so it can read and update CRM records. Covers the connected app to create, the client credential fields, and the host to allow.
- [Connect Sentry](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/sentry.md): Connect Sentry to Claude Tag so it can pull errors and stack traces into threads. Covers the dedicated account to create, the token fields, and the URL to allow.
- [Connect Snowflake](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/snowflake.md): Connect Snowflake to Claude Tag so it can run read-only queries on your warehouse. Covers the dedicated user to create, the access token field, and the host to allow.
- [Connect Stripe](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/stripe.md): Connect Stripe to Claude Tag so it can answer billing and subscription questions. Covers the dedicated account to create, the key fields, and the URL to allow.
- [Connect Vercel](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/connections/vercel.md): Connect Vercel to Claude Tag so it can check deployment status and logs. Covers the dedicated account to create, the token fields, and the URL to allow.
- [Federated agent access](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/federated-access/overview.md): Claude Tag proves its identity to your systems with a short-lived signed token instead of a credential stored in Claude. Learn how the token works and which of the four connection types to use.
- [Connect a gateway](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/federated-access/connect-a-gateway.md): Connect a gateway you run so Claude Tag can call your internal services with a short-lived identity token instead of a stored credential. Covers what the gateway must check, how to register it in the console, and how to verify the connection.
- [Connect an AWS role](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/federated-access/aws.md): Let Claude sign in to an IAM role in your AWS account with a short-lived identity token instead of stored access keys. Covers the identity provider and trust policy to create in AWS, how to connect the role in the console, and how to verify the connection in CloudTrail.
- [Connect a Google Cloud identity](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/federated-access/gcp.md): Let Claude call Google Cloud through workload identity federation with a short-lived identity token instead of a service account key. Covers the pool, provider, and IAM grants to create, with or without a service account, and how to connect the identity in the console.
- [Connect an authorization server](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/federated-access/authorization-server.md): Let Claude exchange a short-lived identity token for an access token from an OAuth 2.0 authorization server you run, then call your APIs with it. Covers what your token endpoint receives and must check, what it returns, and how to register it in the console.
- [Identity token reference](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/federated-access/token-reference.md): The claims, issuer, signing keys, lifetime, and subject format of the identity token Claude Tag presents to a gateway, cloud provider, or authorization server.
- [Limits for federated agent access](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/federated-access/limits.md): Counts, lengths, lifetimes, and unsupported configurations for Claude Tag's federated agent access: gateways, AWS roles, Google Cloud identities, and authorization servers.
- [Troubleshoot federated agent access](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/federated-access/troubleshooting.md): Errors from Claude Tag's federated agent access and what fixes each: console dialog messages, requests Claude reports as blocked or failed, and rejections your gateway, AWS, Google Cloud, or authorization server records.
- [Configure per-channel access](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/attach-to-scope.md): Choose which Slack workspaces and channels a Claude Tag bundle applies to, attach bundles to channels by name, and see how access stacks when bundles overlap.
- [Restrict where Claude Tag operates](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/restrict-access.md): Claude Tag responds only where it has been added and addressed. See who can invoke it, what changes in guest and Slack Connect channels, the per-scope version setting, how to limit it to chosen channels, how to delegate administration or a channel's setup, and how to quiet or remove it.
- [Manage workspaces and versions](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/workspaces.md): Connect more Slack workspaces or an Enterprise Grid to Claude Tag, choose which Claude Tag version each channel uses, and disconnect a workspace.
- [Use Claude Tag at a healthcare organization](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/healthcare.md): Claude Tag is not covered by Anthropic's Business Associate Agreement. Configure it so protected health information never reaches a channel, direct message, or tool Claude can read: limit Claude to approved channels, turn off direct messages, and connect only PHI-free tools. Also covers what to do i…
- [Customize Claude Tag](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/customize.md): Claude Tag is customized per channel and workspace (a scope), not per user. See what admins set in claude.ai, what anyone can change from the channel, and what stays fixed.
- [Claude Tag settings map](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/concepts/settings-map.md): Claude Tag settings map: the admin page for access and behavior, the usage page for spend limits, the in-Slack Configure link for channel instructions, and personal connectors for DMs and your own tasks in channels. Claude Managed Agents is configured separately on the Claude Platform.
- [Set up a skills repository Claude can update](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/skills-repo.md): Put your org's Claude Tag skills in a git repository with auto-sync, grant Claude write access, and Claude can open pull requests to improve its own skills from what it learns in channels.
- [Review what Claude Tag has done](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/audit.md): Claude Tag actions appear under its own service accounts in each connected tool's audit log. See what the Activity page covers, how to trace an action to its source, and where each connected tool keeps logs.
- [Attribute costs to users](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/attribute-costs.md): Pull channel spend per Slack user from the Claude Enterprise Analytics API for showback or chargeback reporting, and see how Claude's work is attributed to people.
- [Troubleshoot Claude Tag setup](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/troubleshooting.md): Error messages from Claude Tag setup and what fixes each. Covers permission mismatches, GitHub access gaps, session start failures, and account errors.
- [Network requirements](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/network-requirements.md): Claude Tag reaches your services from a published egress range, over HTTP and HTTPS only. See the IP block to allowlist and how the allowlist relates to the allowed-websites setting on a connection.
- [Migrate from the earlier Claude in Slack](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/admins/migrate-from-earlier.md): Claude Tag replaces the earlier per-user Claude in Slack app in place. See what changes, what stays, how the version is chosen per channel, and what existing users notice.
- [Get started](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/users/getting-started.md): Claude Tag works in your Slack channels. See how to check it's on, send your first message, what it can read, and why DMs work differently.

- [Commands Claude Tag understands](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/users/commands.md): A few exact, bang-prefixed words after an @-mention run a fixed action instead of starting a normal turn: see the command list, get the link to a channel's settings page, restart a stuck or wrong-context session, check whether Claude is still working in a thread or channel, mute or unmute a thread,…

- [Good habits for working with Claude Tag](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/users/good-habits.md): Name the outcome, give every task a definition of done, and pick the right channel. See how to write tasks Claude can finish and how to keep many threads reviewable.
- [Set up routines](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/users/proactivity.md): Claude Tag runs routines you set up from a channel. See scheduled jobs, channel watching, pull request subscriptions, where results post, and how to pause them.

- [Claude Science](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/overview.md): Anthropic's AI workbench for rigorous science.
- [Get started](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/get-started.md): Install Claude Science on macOS, Windows, or Linux, sign in with your Claude account, and run your first analysis.
- [Claude Science in its own window on macOS](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/mac-app-window.md): Keep working when Claude Science switches to its own window on a Mac: open, quit, and update it, and turn macOS permissions back on.
- [Update Claude Science](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/update-claude-science.md): Install the latest version of Claude Science on Mac, Windows, or Linux, and get past an Update required message or an update that fails.
- [Run on a remote Linux server](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/run-on-remote-linux-server.md): Install Claude Science on a cloud VM or lab server and use it from your own browser through an SSH tunnel.
- [Core concepts](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/core-concepts.md): A project groups related sessions and the artifacts they produce.
- [Example gallery](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery.md): Browse nine example prompts from nine fields of science, each the start of a complete analysis in Claude Science.
- [Genetic drift in a bottle: Buri's 107 fruit-fly populations](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery/bio-drift.md): Simulate 107 bottles of 16 fruit flies drifting by chance alone and compare them with Peter Buri's real bottles (1956).
- [A titration curve from the full equilibrium: which indicator finds the equivalence point?](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery/chem-titration.md): Solve the full equilibrium for 25.0 mL of 0.100 M acetic acid as 0.100 M NaOH is added, without the usual shortcuts.
- [A first Kaplan–Meier curve: the 1963 leukemia trial of 6-MP](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery/clin-km.md): Compare 6-MP against placebo with Kaplan–Meier curves from 42 remission times typed into the prompt.
- [PageRank on a web of 11 pages: why 1 good link beats 6 weak ones](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery/cs-pagerank-tiny.md): Follow a random surfer on Wikipedia's 11-page example until the numbers settle, and reproduce all 11 published values to 0.1 point.
- [A first finite-element model: a clamped steel ruler bends and vibrates](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery/eng-beam.md): Split a 300 mm steel ruler clamped at one end into 4 beam elements and check its bending under 1 N and its first 3 vibration modes against beam theory.
- [A first X-ray diffraction pattern: why silicon shows 6 peaks and salt 9](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery/mat-xrd.md): Simulate the X-ray powder patterns of silicon and table salt and label every peak with Bragg's law.
- [The Ulam spiral: are the primes' diagonal streaks real?](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery/math-ulam.md): Compare the share of primes per diagonal on Ulam's 1963 spiral of 1 to 40,401 against as many random odd numbers.
- [The double slit, one electron at a time](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery/phys-doubleslit.md): Rebuild the picture of Tonomura's 1989 experiment with an ideal double slit: each electron lands as 1 random dot, yet fringes 10.7 µm apart build up.
- [Schelling's segregation model: ask for 30% same-color neighbors, end up with 75%](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery/soc-schelling-small.md): Ask for 30% same-color neighbors, end up with about 75%: the textbook computer version of Thomas Schelling's 1971 idea.
- [Safeguards](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/safeguards.md): What happens when a model's safeguards flag a message, how to switch models automatically, and how to choose a use case under the Life Sciences Verification Program (beta).
- [Auto mode](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/auto-mode.md): Auto mode lets Claude Science run code and call connectors without stopping to ask about every step.
- [Use Claude Science on more than one computer](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/multiple-computers.md): What to expect when you sign in on another computer, or under another sign-in on the same computer.
- [Artifacts in Claude Science](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/artifacts.md): Artifacts in Claude Science are files Claude saves into a project, such as figures, datasets, and reports. Open, version, trace, and delete them.
- [Comments](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/comments.md): Comments in Claude Science pin a note to a specific part of an artifact, such as selected text or a point on a figure, and send the note to Claude.
- [The reviewer](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/the-reviewer.md): A built-in verification step that independently re-reads Claude's recent responses, the approved plan, saved artifacts, and the execution record, then checks whether its claims match what ran.

- [Connectors and skills](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/connectors-and-skills.md): Connectors give Claude access to external data sources during an analysis.
- [Remote compute clusters](https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/remote-compute-clusters.md): Connect a machine you can reach over SSH (a lab workstation or an HPC login node) so Claude can run jobs on it.

- [Claude for Government administrator guide](https://claude.com/docs/government/overview.md): Set up and manage Claude for Government for your agency: how tenants, organizations, users, seats, and credits fit together.
- [Moving from Claude for Government Web](https://claude.com/docs/government/moving-from-web.md): Find answers to the questions agencies ask most often when moving from Claude for Government Web to Claude Desktop.
- [Video walkthroughs for administrators](https://claude.com/docs/government/video-walkthroughs.md): Watch short narrated walkthroughs of setting up and running Claude for Government for your agency.
- [Claude for Government changelog](https://claude.com/docs/government/changelog.md): Release notes for Claude for Government
- [Tenant administration](https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/overview.md): Manage the settings that apply across your whole agency: organizations, identity and sign-in, and how seats are distributed and spend caps are set.
- [Tenant setup wizard](https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/setup-wizard.md): Set up a new tenant in order: verify a domain, connect single sign-on, add an organization, give it seats, and add the routing rule that lets people sign in.
- [Readiness](https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/readiness.md): Readiness checks for your tenant and its organizations: what the checks on domains, routing rules, sign-in failures, and billing mean, and who clears them.
- [Organizations](https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/organizations.md): See every organization in your tenant, open an organization's admin view, add an organization and get it ready for people, and copy user email addresses.
- [Identity and access](https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access.md): Verify domains, connect single sign-on and SCIM, write the routing rules that place people in organizations, and look up what a sign-in error page means.
- [Tenant restrictions](https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/tenant-restrictions.md): Restrict which Claude for Government tenants can be reached from your agency's network by having your network proxy inject an allowlist header.
- [Seats](https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/seats.md): Divide each billing account's seat pool among the organizations it funds, and see who can change an allocation and why a change is refused.
- [Billing](https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/credits.md): See each billing account's credit balance and set per-organization spend caps, with what a cap counts, what it stops, and when a change takes effect.
- [Config at the tenant level](https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/configuration.md): Set tenant-wide defaults for product behavior, lock settings so organizations can't change them, and preview how a change affects each organization.
- [Admins](https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/admins.md): Tenant administrator access: what it grants, who can be added, how to add or remove an administrator, and the safeguards on the list.
- [Organization administration](https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/overview.md): Manage the people, seats, and settings for a single organization within your agency: users, roles, seat tiers, usage, billing, and Config.
- [Setup wizard](https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/setup-wizard.md): Setup wizard for a new organization: how to open it, and what the seat tiers, seats and credits, products, and finish steps cover.
- [Readiness](https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/readiness.md): Readiness checks for your organization: what the checks on credits, spend caps, seats, seat tiers, models, and products mean, and who can clear each one.
- [Users](https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/users.md): Find a user, change their role or seat tier, sign them out everywhere, check and reset their usage limits, and see what each organization role can do.
- [Seats](https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/seats.md): See how many seats of each tier your organization holds and how many are assigned, and how new and unassigned users get a seat tier.
- [Seat tiers](https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers.md): Seat tiers set which Claude models a user can access and how much they can spend. Organization owners create and manage their own seat tiers.
- [Group mappings](https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/provisioning.md): Map directory groups to seat tiers and roles in your organization, and see how mappings are applied and what a deactivation in your directory does.
- [Analytics](https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/analytics.md): Review your organization's requests, tokens, spend, active users, top users, and credit balance over time, and download the data as CSV files for reporting.
- [Analytics API](https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/analytics-api.md): The Analytics API returns your organization's token usage and estimated cost by day, hour, member, product, or model. A Primary Owner creates the key.
- [Compliance API](https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/compliance-api.md): Stream your organization's audit events into a SIEM or log management system.
- [Admin API keys](https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/admin-api-keys.md): Admin API keys let organization owners give a script read-only access to audit events, and let Primary Owners give it access to usage reports.
- [Billing](https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/billing.md): See the balance your organization spends from, the spend caps set on it, and its seats, and what happens as the billing account's balance runs low.
- [Config at the organization level](https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/configuration.md): Set product settings for everyone in your organization on the Config page, and see how connectors and plugins inherited from your tenant behave there.
- [How Config works](https://claude.com/docs/government/config/overview.md): Config levels in Claude for Government: how tenant, directory group, and organization settings combine, what locks do, and when changes reach members.
- [Available settings](https://claude.com/docs/government/config/settings.md): Config page settings in Claude for Government, such as session timeouts, network and folder access, tool approvals, connectors, plugins, telemetry, and updates.
- [Manage plugins and connectors](https://claude.com/docs/government/config/plugins-and-connectors.md): Upload plugins in Claude for Government: archive rules, size limits, skills packaged as plugins, the Runs code marker, install behavior, updates, and removal.
- [Connectors](https://claude.com/docs/government/connectors/overview.md): Connectors let tenant administrators and organization owners add their agency's MCP servers: who gets them, authentication, OAuth redirect URIs, tool policy.
- [Set up the Microsoft 365 connector](https://claude.com/docs/government/connectors/microsoft-365.md): Register a Microsoft Entra application for the Microsoft 365 connector in Claude Desktop, choose its read and write permissions, and fix sign-in errors.
- [Security and data handling](https://claude.com/docs/government/security/security-and-data-handling.md): Review how Claude for Government handles data: sandbox isolation, network traffic, approvals, connector credentials, telemetry, web search, and local storage.
- [Connect Claude Desktop to Claude for Government](https://claude.com/docs/government/deploy-desktop/configure.md): Connect Claude Desktop to Claude for Government: the bootstrap URL, device profiles for macOS, Windows, and Linux, network hosts, updates, and troubleshooting.
- [Windows fleet checklist](https://claude.com/docs/government/deploy-desktop/windows-checklist.md): Windows device, MSIX installer, application control, and virtualization checks to make before you deploy Claude Desktop for Claude for Government.
- [Deploy Claude for Microsoft 365 in Claude for Government](https://claude.com/docs/government/deploy-microsoft-365/configure.md): Download the Claude for Microsoft 365 manifest from your Claude for Government host and deploy the add-in to users from the Microsoft 365 admin center.
- [Video walkthroughs for Claude Desktop](https://claude.com/docs/government/desktop/video-walkthroughs.md): Watch short narrated walkthroughs of signing in to Claude Desktop with Claude for Government, bringing your work over, and finding your way around the app.
- [Import your data from Claude for Government Web](https://claude.com/docs/government/desktop/import.md): Copy your conversations, projects, and files from Claude for Government Web into Claude Desktop.
- [Plugins in Claude Desktop](https://claude.com/docs/government/desktop/plugins.md): Find, install, create, and remove plugins in Claude Desktop for Claude for Government, and understand what plugins add in this deployment.
- [Skills in Claude Desktop](https://claude.com/docs/government/desktop/skills.md): Skills in Claude Desktop for Claude for Government: where they come from, how to create and manage your own, and how administrators distribute them.
- [Models in Claude Desktop](https://claude.com/docs/government/desktop/models.md): Switch models in Claude Desktop on Claude for Government, see what the 1M context window does, and find what controls which models you see.
- [Connect Claude Code to Claude for Government](https://claude.com/docs/government/deploy-claude-code/configure.md): Connect the Claude Code command-line tool to Claude for Government with managed settings on macOS, Windows, and Linux, and confirm a device is set up.
- [Your account](https://claude.com/docs/government/account/overview.md): Check your own account details, usage limits, and active sessions in the Claude for Government web portal.
- [Account](https://claude.com/docs/government/account/profile.md): Check the email, organization, role, and seat tier on your Claude for Government account, who to ask to change each one, and what to do with no seat.
- [Usage](https://claude.com/docs/government/account/usage.md): Check how much of your Claude allowance you have used and when it resets, and what to do when you hit a usage limit or your organization runs out of credits.
- [Sessions](https://claude.com/docs/government/account/sessions.md): See every place you are signed in to Claude for Government, sign any of them out, and check how long sessions last and what ends them.
